_comment: The message you decided to tell. Rewrite these six for your own positioning; ids are stable, labels are what humans read.

elements.label: The problem
elements.definition: Names the operating pain the buyer lives with, before describing any product.

elements.label: The category
elements.definition: Places the product in the category you chose to compete in, rather than describing it as a tool or a feature.

elements.label: See what is happening
elements.definition: The buyer stops chasing people for status; the system shows the current state.

elements.label: Be told, not go looking
elements.definition: Problems are surfaced to the responsible person instead of waiting to be discovered.

elements.label: What no other system can do
elements.definition: The specific reason the incumbent stack cannot produce this, stated concretely.

elements.label: Value that lasts
elements.definition: Why the gain compounds instead of fading after the rollout.

framing_pair.why: Reported separately because a coverage score is structurally blind to it: every promise can land while the frame around them is still the old pitch.

expected_by_call_type._why: Elements that are the point of that kind of meeting. They still count for coverage — the rep did say them — but they are never reported as 'what worked', because praising someone for doing the thing the meeting exists for reads as noise and costs the whole message its credibility. Missing one of these is the finding, not delivering it. Edit this for your own funnel.
